name: external_peg_nominal_ppo_v10_grasp_retention_continuation
supersession_reason: The v9 nominal controller plateaued: its best checkpoint is at 62,259,200 of a 75,000,000 budget, and a 512-episode characterization found 84 of 85 emergent failures are the peg grasped and then lost before reaching within 8 cm of the hole. Those failures occur before the contact-rich part of the task, so they cannot support a recovery benchmark. This continuation fine-tunes from the frozen v9 checkpoint at a reduced learning rate to test whether grasp retention improves and failures move toward the hole.
purpose: Establish whether a stronger nominal controller produces a diverse emergent failure distribution. This is a precondition for a non-scripted recovery benchmark, not a recovery result.

allocation_gate.note: Frozen before training. The continuation is retained only if it improves nominal competence and diversifies emergent failures; either check failing means the non-scripted benchmark route is not opened on this controller.

claim_boundary: Nominal competence and emergent failure diversity only. No recovery, routing, or shortcut-audit claim follows from this configuration. The 425000000 and 429000000 families remain unopened.
